summary: Enterprise AI in 2026 is dominated by cloud-native model API aggregators that let corporations consume foundation models (GPT, Claude, Llama, Gemini, Mistral and more) through secure, governed managed endpoints where data stays inside the company's existing cloud boundary. There is no single winner — the best fit is usually dictated by a company's existing cloud footprint, compliance posture, and desired model breadth, with AWS Bedrock leading on model choice, Azure OpenAI on frontier OpenAI models, and Google Vertex AI on Gemini and MLOps depth. Secondary players like Snowflake Cortex, IBM watsonx, Oracle Cloud AI, and Cloudflare Workers AI serve specialized data-gravity, regulated-industry, and edge-inference niches.
why_enterprises_use_aggregators: Data residency and privacy: prompts, completions, and fine-tuning data stay within the company's own cloud tenant/region and are not used to train vendor foundation models, satisfying internal data-governance rules.

Compliance and certifications: aggregators inherit the cloud provider's SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, FedRAMP, PCI-DSS, and GDPR/EU data-boundary controls, which raw vendor APIs often cannot match out of the box.
Consolidated billing and existing cloud contracts: usage draws down committed spend (EDP/MACC/enterprise agreements), appears on one invoice, and avoids new vendor procurement and security reviews.
Unified security and identity: native integration with IAM/Entra ID/VPC, private networking, KMS encryption, and centralized audit logging replaces managing separate API keys per model vendor.

Model portability and single API: one abstraction layer gives access to many competing models (Claude, Llama, Mistral, GPT, Gemini), reducing lock-in and letting teams swap models without re-architecting.

platforms.name: AWS Bedrock
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-token (on-demand) plus Provisioned Throughput reserved capacity for guaranteed throughput; batch inference offers discounts.
platforms.best_for: Companies already on AWS wanting the widest model choice behind one governed API with deep IAM and VPC integration.

platforms.name: Azure OpenAI Service / Azure AI Foundry
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-token plus Provisioned Throughput Units (PTUs) for reserved, predictable capacity; draws down Microsoft committed spend.
key_features: Frontier OpenAI models with enterprise SLAs
Content filtering and Azure Monitor audit logs
platforms.best_for: Microsoft-first enterprises needing frontier OpenAI models with tight M365, Entra, and Azure governance integration.

platforms.name: Google Vertex AI Model Garden
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-token/character for on-demand, plus Provisioned Throughput sold in GSUs (Generative Scale Units) for reserved throughput (e.g., ~67,250 tokens/sec for 25 GSUs of Gemini 2.5 Flash).
key_features: Native Gemini plus multi-vendor Model Garden
platforms.best_for: Google Cloud shops and data/ML-centric teams wanting Gemini plus deep MLOps and grounding on BigQuery data.

platforms.name: Snowflake Cortex AI
platforms.pricing: Consumption-based, billed in Snowflake credits by model and token usage; no separate model-vendor contracts.
key_features: LLMs run next to governed data in the Snowflake perimeter
SQL / Python (Cortex functions) access to models
Role-based access control and row/column governance
Cortex Analyst and Cortex Search for RAG
No data movement outside the warehouse
platforms.best_for: Data teams that want to run LLMs directly against governed warehouse data without moving it out of Snowflake.

platforms.name: IBM watsonx.ai
platforms.pricing: Subscription plus consumption (Resource Units); available as SaaS, on-prem, and hybrid (Cloud Pak for Data).
key_features: On-prem / hybrid and air-gapped deployment options
watsonx.governance for model risk and compliance
watsonx Orchestrate for cross-platform AI agents
platforms.best_for: Highly regulated industries (finance, government, healthcare) needing hybrid/on-prem deployment with strong AI governance.

platforms.name: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) Generative AI
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-token on-demand plus dedicated AI clusters for reserved capacity; integrates with Oracle enterprise agreements.
key_features: Dedicated AI clusters for isolated capacity
Integration with Oracle Fusion/Database and 23ai vector search
platforms.best_for: Oracle-centric enterprises embedding GenAI into Fusion apps and Oracle Database workloads, including sovereign cloud needs.

platforms.name: Cloudflare Workers AI
platforms.pricing: Usage-based (Neurons / per-request pricing) with a free tier; AI Gateway bills for caching, rate-limiting, and observability.
key_features: Serverless inference on global edge network
AI Gateway for caching, logging, and multi-provider routing
Vectorize vector database and R2 integration
platforms.best_for: Developers building low-latency, globally distributed AI apps and teams wanting an edge gateway in front of multiple model providers.

platforms.name: Databricks Mosaic AI (Model Serving)
platforms.pricing: Consumption-based (DBUs) for model serving and training; runs within the customer's cloud account (AWS/Azure/GCP).
key_features: Unity Catalog governance and lineage over data and models
Models served next to lakehouse data
AI Gateway for rate limits, logging, and routing
platforms.best_for: Lakehouse-centric enterprises that want to fine-tune and serve models against governed data with strong lineage and MLOps.
